alt: Two pointers on a sorted list. lo starts at the left end and hi at the right end. When their sum is too small, lo moves right; when it is too big, hi moves left; they stop at a pair with the target sum or when they meet.

steps.caption: The list is sorted. `lo` starts at the smallest value and `hi` at the largest; the goal is a pair that adds up to 13.
1 + 11 = 12 is too small. Every partner of 1 is at most 11, so 1 can never reach 13: `lo` moves right.
3 + 11 = 14 is too big. Every partner of 11 is at least 3, so 11 is always too big: `hi` moves left.
3 + 9 = 12 is too small. Every partner of 3 is at most 9, so 3 can never reach 13: `lo` moves right.
4 + 9 is exactly 13: the pair is at indices 2 and 5.
The list is sorted. `lo` starts at the smallest value and `hi` at the largest; the goal is a pair that adds up to 6.
1 + 9 = 10 is too big. Every partner of 9 is at least 1, so 9 is always too big: `hi` moves left.
1 + 8 = 9 is too big. Every partner of 8 is at least 1, so 8 is always too big: `hi` moves left.
1 + 7 = 8 is too big. Every partner of 7 is at least 1, so 7 is always too big: `hi` moves left.
1 + 2 = 3 is too small. Every partner of 1 is at most 2, so 1 can never reach 6: `lo` moves right.
`lo` and `hi` have met, so every pair has been ruled out: no two values add up to 6.
